title: Has household income changed in Multnomah County?
text:
Median household income is one way to track how a community’s finances change. This small project looks at Multnomah County, Oregon, using one ACS estimate for each year from 2010 through 2023.

income <- readr::read_csv("data/median_income.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

ggplot2::ggplot(income, ggplot2::aes(x = year, y = estimate)) +
  ggplot2::geom_line(color = "#28666e", linewidth = 1) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(color = "#28666e", size = 2) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::label_dollar()) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2010, 2023, by = 2)) +
  ggplot2::labs(
    x = "ACS 5-year estimate ending year",
    y = "Median household income",
    caption = paste(
      "Source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates,",
      "table B19013. Values are not adjusted for inflation."
    )
  ) +
  ggplot2::theme_minimal()








Each point is a 5-year estimate, so neighboring points use overlapping years. The margin of error is available in the downloaded data, but is not shown in this first, simple chart.

title: About
text: This site uses the U.S. Census Bureau’s American Community Survey (ACS) 5-year estimates to look at median household income in Multnomah County, Oregon. The series runs from 2010 through 2023; dollar values are not adjusted for inflation, and the 5-year estimates overlap.

title: About
text:
Reproduce the analysis
The download step is separate from the website:

Configure your Census API key for tidycensus in your local R environment. Do not save the key in this repository.
Run Rscript data-raw/download_income.R to create data/median_income.csv.
Run quarto render to rebuild the website. The chart in index.qmd reads that CSV.

The downloader requests ACS table B19013 (median household income) for Multnomah County. The margin of error is included in the CSV.
